cf.title: Fix ReadStream handling when heap rescan strategy changes

input.subject: Fix ReadStream handling when heap rescan strategy changes

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived the critic; the only one raised, maintenance-fit-1, was refuted because the material does not show a field-by-field copy in heapam.c. The proposal is a bug fix for b7b0f3f27241 with a stated defect, a reachable case in core (message #3) and no new user-visible surface. Two reviewers support a separate fix. The result is provisional because the code was not read.

brief.title: Recreate heap scan ReadStream when rescan changes strategy use
brief.problem: Since b7b0f3f27241, heap scans keep their ReadStream across rescans, but initscan() can add or free rs_strategy on a rescan. Enabling the strategy leaves the stream with a NULL strategy and its old queue capacity. Disabling it frees the strategy while the stream still points to it, which an extension can reach but core cannot, per the thread.
brief.proposed_design: On rescan, initscan() ends and recreates the ReadStream when the scan switches between using and not using a buffer access strategy. Ordinary rescans still reset and reuse the existing stream. With instrumentation on, the new stream gets the accumulated statistics back and keeps the maximum capacity seen so far.
user_visible_surface: New TAP test src/test/modules/test_misc/t/016_heap_rescan_strategy.pl, which starts its own cluster.
author_claims: The fix uses only existing ReadStream APIs, so backpatching is easier than with the proposed read_stream_set_strategy() API.
Against the read_stream_set_strategy() approach, the difference was below 0.15 microseconds per rescan, so performance favors neither.
An extension can reach the dangling pointer by starting a large seqscan with allow_strat = true, then calling table_rescan_set_params() with allow_strat = false.
brief.thread_state: Nazir Bilal Yavuz supports a separate fix and prefers this simpler approach for backpatching; shihao zhong agreed an extension can reach the bug and asked to say so in the commit message. Open: whether to commit the costly 0002 test, and a cosmetic condition rewrite.
unclear: The commit message does not list the back branches the fix targets.
The patch prose does not say why read_stream.c changes if only existing ReadStream APIs are used.
No one says how stream recreation interacts with scans in progress, such as parallel or sync scans.
The thread does not say whether any known extension calls table_rescan_set_params() this way.
search_queries: bulk read strategy sequential scan rescan

refuted.title: Carrying stream statistics across recreated streams is a hand-kept copy
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a counter or a high-water mark to ReadStream instrumentation, and the recreate path in initscan() does not copy it. After a rescan that switches strategy, EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) shows reset or wrong stream statistics. No test fails, so a user reading a misleading plan reports it much later.
refuted.argument: The commit message says the fix reattaches accumulated statistics and keeps the maximum capacity across streams. That is per-field state copied from one stream to the next. The patch also touches read_stream.c, though message #1 says only existing ReadStream APIs are used, and the prose does not say what changed there. If the copy is done field by field in heapam.c, every future instrumentation field must also be added there by hand.
refuted.author_must_show: What changes in read_stream.c, and does it keep the statistics carry-over inside read_stream.c so that new instrumentation fields cannot be missed?

critic.reasoning: The scenario depends on a field-by-field copy in heapam.c, which the material does not show. The commit message says the fix reattaches the accumulated statistics, and the patch touches read_stream.c, so the carry-over may already live there.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch changes read_stream.c, and the reported dangling pointer is reached by extensions that call table_rescan_set_params().

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The CommitFest entry targets stable branches, and message #1 gives easier backpatching as a reason for this approach.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The recreate path carries instrumentation statistics and maximum capacity from the old stream to the new one.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: initscan() runs on every heap rescan, though the stream is recreated only when strategy use switches.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which back branches does the fix target, and does the read_stream.c change alter any exported struct or function that those branches must keep ABI-stable?
What changes in read_stream.c, given that message #1 says the fix uses only existing ReadStream APIs?
Does the statistics and maximum-capacity carry-over live inside read_stream.c, so that a new instrumentation field cannot be missed in heapam.c?
Is recreating the stream in initscan() safe for parallel scans and sync scans, where scan position state is shared or reported?
Should the 0002 TAP test, which starts its own cluster, go into the tree, or is there a cheaper way to cover the strategy switch?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows the ReadStream and AIO code and the heap scan setup in heapam.c would have to own it. The visible thread and the CommitFest entry do not identify any participant as a committer.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a backpatched change to heap rescan and ReadStream lifetime in the stable branches, including any ABI effect of the read_stream.c change, for the life of those branches.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted a patch and a test and asked for review in message #1. Only the first 3 of 6 messages are shown, so there is no further sign either way.

priority.reason: The fix is a small patch to two files that corrects a defect from b7b0f3f27241. Core reaches only the stale NULL strategy case with extra buffer pollution (message #3); the freed-pointer case needs an extension.

provisional_note: Without the code, the read_stream.c change, its ABI effect on back branches, and the place where the statistics carry-over lives could not be checked. Stream recreation during parallel or sync scans also could not be checked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Eagerly evict bulkwrite strategy ring
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make the BAS_BULKWRITE buffer access strategy flush several dirty buffers in its ring at once, skipping buffers whose flush would require a WAL flush. This was meant as a first step toward combining writes and issuing them asynchronously, and gave about 15-20% faster parallel COPY FROM.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry after moving all of its patches into the patch set in the separate write combining thread, so the work continues there. No reviewer objected to the design; reviews found only code issues, which the author fixed. Earlier the author noted that the gain from this patch alone might not justify committing it.
matched_queries: bulk read strategy sequential scan rescan
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: All of the patches that implement the bulkwrite eager flush functionality are included in the patch set being actively updated in this thread [1] on write combining.

precedents_retrieved.title: Implement TODOs for index operator strategy number validation
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds strategy number bounds checks to operator class validation for BRIN, GIN, GiST and SP-GiST, implementing TODOs in that code. BRIN and SP-GiST use RTMaxStrategyNumber as the upper limit, GiST uses a limit computed from the Geo* constants, and GIN keeps its existing limit of 63.
precedents_retrieved.objection: GiST, SP-GiST and BRIN set amstrategies = 0, so strategy numbers are defined by each opclass, and the new checks would make amvalidate() reject valid custom opclasses. RTMaxStrategyNumber is not a general limit for these access methods, and the Geo* constants apply only to the built-in GiST point implementation. The author withdrew the patch for rework.
matched_queries: bulk read strategy sequential scan rescan
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
For example, a custom SP-GiST opclass can use strategy 31 if its support
functions understand it, but this patch would make amvalidate() reject
it.

precedents_retrieved.title: New strategies for freezing, advancing relfrozenxid early
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch series lets each VACUUM choose a skipping strategy and a freezing strategy at the start, using a snapshot of the visibility map, so that unfrozen all-visible pages do not pile up until an aggressive VACUUM. A new vacuum_freeze_strategy_threshold GUC and reloption, default 4GB, makes VACUUM freeze eagerly in tables above that size, and a further patch avoids allocating new MultiXactIds during freezing.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund posted a short test with transient data, cited in message #98, in which autovacuum wrote about 1.5x to 7x as much WAL with eager freezing. He argued that table size cannot tell VACUUM whether eager freezing is a good idea, and said he saw no alternative to reverting the commit. Robert Haas agreed that the scenario is common and objected to large behavior changes based on limited evidence. Peter Geoghegan reverted the commit and withdrew the whole series.
matched_queries: bulk read strategy sequential scan rescan
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The actual scenario he came up with is three lines of SQL, and it's nothing remotely obscure. That kind of thing is going to happen *all the time*.

precedents_retrieved.title: Detect shared buffer access violations using mprotect()
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a compile-time option (-DMPROTECT_BUFFER) that uses mprotect() to mark shared buffers read-only or read-write according to pin and content-lock state, so that violations of shared buffer access rules are caught. The patch came out of a discussion of places that modify shared buffers without holding the content lock.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane asked that the patch be restructured so that bad accesses can be caught with either Valgrind or mprotect depending on compile options, using macros such as ProtectBuffer() that expand to nothing when the feature is disabled instead of inline #ifdef blocks. He also raised the concern that buffers are not reliably aligned on system page boundaries. The author did not address this feedback before the commitfest ended, so Andres Freund marked the entry returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It'd be better to
set things up so that the patch adds support for catching bad accesses
with either valgrind or mprotect, according to compile options.

precedents_retrieved.title: Don't shut down Gather[Merge] early under Limit.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Don't shut down Gather[Merge] early under Limit.
Reverted commit(s): Fix buffer usage stats for parallel nodes.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Revert part of commit 19df1702f5.

Early shutdown was added by that commit so that we could collect
statistics from workers, but unfortunately, it interacted badly with
rescans.  The problem is that we ended up destroying the parallel context
which is required for rescans.  This leads to rescans of a Limit node over
a Gather node to produce unpredictable results as it tries to access
destroyed parallel context.  By reverting the early shutdown code, we
might lose statistics in some cases of Limit over Gather [Merge], but that
will require further study to fix.

precedents_retrieved.title: Reorder tablespaces for streaming basebackups
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changed the order of the tar streams sent by the BASE_BACKUP replication command so that the main data directory comes first, which puts backup_label at the beginning of a combined tarball for third-party tools. After review it was narrowed to apply only when WAL is not included, because in fetch mode the WAL files are appended to the main tarball, which must therefore stay last.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Fujii Masao pointed out that BASE_BACKUP already sends the start WAL location in its first result set, before any tar data, so reading backup_label early is not needed for that purpose; further information could be added to that result set instead. He also said that running BASE_BACKUP through psql is not a good approach and that a proper client or an extension of pg_basebackup should be used. Michael Paquier agreed that the patch was therefore not useful and proposed dropping it, and the author marked it Rejected as the consensus.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
In my first reviews of the patch, I completely forgot the fact that
BASE_BACKUP does send the start LSN of the backup in the first result
set, so the patch proposed is actually rather useless because the data
you are looking for is already at hand.

precedents_retrieved.title: Support SK_SEARCHNULL / SK_SEARCHNOTNULL for heap-only scans
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes heap scans honor SK_SEARCHNULL and SK_SEARCHNOTNULL scan keys in HeapKeyTest(), which skey.h documents as supported only for index scans. The goal was convenience for extensions that scan tables directly without SPI; a later follow-up by Jacob Champion added planner pushdown of IS [NOT] NULL quals into Seq Scan as scan keys.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas saw no benefit in heapam support alone and asked that nodeSeqScan.c use it, with performance results, and that the table AM API get an 'amsearchnulls' field. The author wanted to defer the executor part to a later patch, so Heikki marked the entry Returned with Feedback. The later executor and planner patches got no visible review before the entry closed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Ok, I don't think this patch on its own is a good idea, without the
other parts, so I'll mark this as Returned with Feedback in the commitfest.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve documentation for pg_upgrade, standbys and rsync
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch rewrites the pg_upgrade documentation for upgrading standbys with rsync: it recommends rsync --relative, updates the version numbers and paths in the examples, and adds a reminder to create standby.signal. Later versions also add SQL steps to drop leftover temporary tables and truncate unlogged tables before the rsync, and reorder the preparation steps.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Stephen Frost argued that this procedure is too hard to get right in an rsync command or a documented procedure, and that a tool should replace it. He proposed moving the text out of the documentation to a wiki. Robert Haas found the new order of the preparation steps confusing. The author saw no agreement and withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
To be more explicit though- we should write a tool to do this.  We
shouldn't try to document a way to do it because it's hard to get right.

precedents_retrieved.title: Set default transactions to read-only at servers start in pg_upgrade
precedents_retrieved.summary: pg_upgrade would start the old and new servers with default_transaction_read_only set, so that background workers from extensions cannot write to the old cluster during the checks step. A later patch also kept background workers from starting in binary upgrade mode, because such writes can leave the upgraded cluster with invalid xids or multixacts.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last messages, from August 2021, still debate where to block background workers: in bgworker_should_start_now(), in RegisterBackgroundWorker(), or not in the backend at all. They also ask whether extensions could fail when their workers do not run. No message explains the withdrawal in December 2021.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P10] shares only the word rescan: that revert was about Gather destroying a parallel context that rescans still needed, while this patch rebuilds a ReadStream that a rescan has made stale. Message #1 points to an earlier alternative, Yuhang's read_stream_set_strategy() API. The thread reports it as reviewed with no correctness problem found, not rejected, and message #2 prefers this simpler fix for backpatching.

From a standards and compatibility view this is an internal bug fix: it adds no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog object, dump state or psql behaviour, and existing queries keep their plans and results. Without the code, two points cannot be checked: whether the read_stream.c change alters any exported struct or function that back branches must keep ABI-stable, and which branches the fix targets.

The fix changes only per-backend scan state: when the ReadStream is recreated and what strategy pointer it holds. It touches no on-disk format, WAL, catalog or wire protocol. The read_stream.c change is not described, so whether it alters a struct that extensions see in back branches cannot be checked without the code.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. It fixes a dangling pointer that only an extension calling table_rescan_set_params() can reach, so no SQL-level user gains a new path. It adds no new object, role, setting, view or default. Stream recreation runs only on a strategy switch, so an unprivileged user gets no new resource-use lever.

The fix itself fits core and has no hot-path cost. Ordinary rescans reuse the stream, and message #5 measured a difference of less than 0.15 microseconds per rescan. The only concern from this angle is the instrumentation carry-over.

This is a bug fix for a ReadStream that keeps a stale or freed strategy across heap rescans, and no existing feature, extension or setting avoids it. The only alternative, read_stream_set_strategy() from another thread, is a competing unmerged fix, and this patch builds on existing ReadStream APIs without adding a second mechanism.

This is a bug fix to b7b0f3f27241, so it needs a reachable defect, not user demand. Core can reach the stale NULL strategy and its extra buffer pollution (message #3), and an extension can reach the freed strategy pointer (messages #4 and #6). Two reviewers agree a separate fix is worth doing, and the fix adds no user-visible surface. Whether to commit the costly 0002 test is a test-cost question outside the demand angle.
